thread.title: Smartphones: Samsung Leads Huawei, Apple in Q2

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Smartphones: Samsung Leads Huawei, Apple in Q2
text:
Photo: Bloomberg News By David Marino-Nachison Aug. 1, 2018 11:32 a.m. ET Global smartphone shipments slid in the second quarter, according to new estimates, representing the third consecutive quarter of declines.
Total shipments for the quarter were 342 million, IDC said Tuesday night, down 1.8% from 348.2 million in the same quarter a year ago.
Newsletter Sign-up Samsung saw shipments fall more than 10% in Q2 but retained the top spot in total shipments with 71.5 million, according to IDC, representing a nearly 21% market share. Huawei took second, which IDC said made Q2 the first quarter since 2010 in which Apple (AAPL) wasn’t in the first or second position.
That could change in the second half, with an iPhone refresh expected later this year. “Apple moved into the top position each of the last two holiday quarters following its product refresh, so it’s likely we’ll see continued movement among the top ranked companies in 2018 and beyond,” IDC’s Ryan Reith said in a statement .
Xiaomi and OPPO rounded out the top 5, according to IDC.
Illustration: IDC
Rising average selling prices, seeing as a highlight in Apple’s latest quarterly earnings announcement , were seen among several brands, according to a report from Counterpoint Research .
More About Barron’s Next Learn more about Barron’s Next The Barron’s Next 50 “Major Chinese brands like OPPO, vivo, Huawei are now focusing on increasing their average selling prices through gradually upgrading their portfolio to higher price bands by bringing in features like Artificial Intelligence, bezel-less displays, dual cameras and with innovative industrial design and colors, materials and finishes in the affordable premium segment,” Counterpoint’s Shobhit Srivastava said in a statement.”
Illustration: Counterpoint Research “Consumers remain willing to pay more for premium offerings in numerous markets and they now expect their device to outlast and outperform previous generations of that device which cost considerably less a few years ago,” said IDC’s Anthony Scarsella. “Vendors will need to focus on new innovative features and form factors combined with incentives and promotions to drive growth.”
